summary: Dennis A. Johnson works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes (attested 2012) and was affiliated with its South Asian, Tibetan and Buddhist Studies Library (attested 2022).

Dennis Genpo Merzel is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Southern California and the USC Rossier School of Education, and trained under traditional teacher Taizan Maezumi circa 1972–1995.

Dennis Hirota specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at UC Berkeley (BA circa 1963–1967; MA circa 1967–1969) and Nagoya University (PhD circa 1992–1996). He was a professor at Ryukoku University (circa 1997–2017) and Harvard visiting professor (2008).

Denzaburo Yoshizawa was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji circa 1946–1949. He held academic posts at Tokyo Metropolitan University (circa 1965–1987) and Iryo Sosei University.

Derek F. Maher is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned degrees from Evergreen State College (BA 1987) and the University of Virginia (MA 1994, PhD 2003 under Jeffrey Hopkins), and co-directed East Carolina University's Religious Studies Program (attested 2010).

Dermot Killingley is an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at Merton College, Oxford, and SOAS. He held appointments at the University of Malaya (1961–1968), Newcastle University (Reader, 1970–2000), and the University of Vienna as visiting professor (2008).

Dermott Walsh specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed a BA at Trinity College Dublin (2003), an MA at Leiden University (2009), and a PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles under William M. Bodiford (2018).

Devadatta Ramakrishna Bhandarkar was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as Superintendent of the Archaeological Survey of India's Western Circle (1911–1917) and as Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta (attested 1910).
Dewei Zhang specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia under the supervision of Jinhua Chen (attested 2010).
Dezhung Kunga Gyaltsen studied under the teachers Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Khenpo Shenga.

Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Gaton Ngawang Lekpa and Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse, and participated in a research project at the University of Washington (1960–1972).

Dharmananda Damodar Kosambi was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Harvard University (1926). He held posts at the University of Calcutta (circa 1906–1908), Harvard (circa 1910–1931), University of Saint Petersburg (circa 1929–1930), and Gujarat University.
Dhirendra Mohan Datta was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Calcutta. He held academic posts at Patna College (1928) and the University of Minnesota (1951–1952).
Dhirendra Sharma is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under David Friedman and traditional teacher Surendra Sharma.

Dhivan Thomas Jones is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Richard Gombrich and Margaret Cone. He held teaching posts at the Open University (attested 2017) and the University of Chester (2019).

Di Luo specializes in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Supervised by James Steele for an MA and by Dominic Cheung, Sonya S. Lee, and Bettine Birge for doctoral work, Di Luo earned a PhD from the University of Southern California (attested 2016).

Diana L. Eck is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. Educated at Smith College, SOAS, and Harvard (PhD 1976 under Daniel H. H. Ingalls), she became a professor of comparative religion and Indian studies at Harvard circa 1976.

Diana Lange works in Tibetology, Sinology, and Central Asian studies. Educated at Leipzig, Tibet University, University of Berlin (PhD 2008), and EPHE (habilitation 2018), she held posts at Hamburg, Berlin, and Leipzig, becoming Berlin professor of Central Asian history and cultures (2025).

Diane A. Lichtenstein earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1977). She served as Adjunct Professor of Anthropology at both Baldwin Wallace University and the Cleveland Institute of Art (attested 2005).

Diane E. Riggs specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at UCLA under William M. Bodiford (2010) and has held posts at Kenyon College (attested 2010), Pepperdine University, and Western Michigan University (attested 2017).
